_schema_and_metadata.design_philosophy: Minimalist, respectful, grounded in artisan & collective studio life. All items plain English (<=12 words/sentence). Zero construct exposure to candidates.

assessment_sections.section_2: Game-Based Assessments (GBAs) — 7 Worlds, 14 Candidate Core Interactive Activities + 7 Research Bank Activities

layout_rules.options_placement: Strictly outside the visual graphical tile with clear directive

empathy.name: Empathy
empathy.definition: The capacity to recognize, interpret, and respond sensitively to the emotional and practical needs of others, particularly by reading subtle social and contextual cues.

conscientiousness.name: Conscientiousness
conscientiousness.definition: The tendency to be reliable, methodical, and responsible, characterized by a willingness to verify information under uncertainty and follow through on commitments.

collaborative_spirit.name: Collaborative Spirit
collaborative_spirit.definition: The willingness to share space, synchronize efforts, and adapt one's own pacing or goals to support an interdependent, collective outcome.

emotional_agility.name: Emotional Agility
emotional_agility.definition: The ability to maintain composure, recover quickly from setbacks, and adapt constructively to ambiguous, sudden, or frustrating changes in the environment.

curiosity.name: Curiosity
curiosity.definition: The intrinsic drive to seek out new information, explore alternative perspectives, and engage with the unknown, even when there is no immediate instrumental reward.

creative_initiative.name: Creative Initiative
creative_initiative.definition: The readiness to experiment, iterate, and apply unconventional solutions when standard procedures, rules, or resources fail to solve a problem.

motivation.name: Motivation
motivation.definition: The willingness to sustain voluntary effort, persist through unglamorous or tedious tasks, and go beyond minimum requirements for the benefit of the collective.

overview.scoring_method: Additive trait scoring. Each option contributes 0-3 points across the 7 parameters.

backend_config.instruction_body: You will encounter seven scenarios drawn from real moments across our collective—workshops, exhibitions, editorial curation, and community gatherings. For each situation, consider the context and select the response that feels most natural to you. There are no trick questions or hidden scoring traps; we value genuine, thoughtful perspectives.
backend_config.timing_note: Takes about 5 to 7 minutes. Move at a comfortable, unhurried pace.

frontend_screen_copy.welcome_text: You will read 7 short stories about everyday moments in our studio, workshops, and community events.

step_cards.title: Read the Story
step_cards.text: Each card shares a real situation from the studio.

step_cards.title: Pick Your Choice
step_cards.text: Choose the answer that best matches what you would really do.

step_cards.title: No Trick Questions
step_cards.text: There are no right or wrong answers. Pick what feels honest and natural to you.

frontend_screen_copy.time_and_controls: 7 stories · Takes about 6 to 8 minutes · Go at your own comfortable pace · Tap an option or press keys 1–4.

scenarios.title: Missing Paintings Before Opening
scenarios.setup_narrative: The art exhibition opens in 2 hours. One artist's paintings have not arrived yet. The exhibition lead is very stressed while fixing the hall lights.

options.text: Quietly take over setup tasks and work quickly to give the lead space.
Suggest rearranging the room layout right now to hide the empty wall.
Go to the lead and ask directly how you can help them right now.
Start calling contacts yourself to find the artist or get backup art.

scenarios.title: Two Artists, One Quiet Corner
scenarios.setup_narrative: An artist, Faizan, is upset because his artwork was placed near the noisy entrance. He wants a quiet corner. Another artist, Meher, is already in the quiet corner and is happy there.

options.text: Bring Faizan and Meher together to talk and find an agreement.
Politely but firmly keep the original floor plan so things stay fair.
Walk through the building to find an empty, unused corner for Faizan.
Offer to stand near Faizan's artwork yourself to keep the crowd quiet.

scenarios.title: An Unexpected School Visit
scenarios.setup_narrative: A school teacher arrives without notice with 15 students. The room is still messy, with loose cables on the floor.

options.text: Gather the students in the entrance hall for a quick question-and-answer talk.
Politely remind the teacher of the opening time, but take their details to book a tour later.
Rope off a safe corner of the room and watch the students yourself.
Show them one piece of art safely without disturbing the setup work.

scenarios.title: Someone Wants to Speak
scenarios.setup_narrative: During a group discussion, Zara, a new member, leans forward to speak but pulls back nervously.

options.text: Wait for a quiet moment and gently invite her to speak.
Notice what she is interested in and bring those topics up for the whole group.
Talk to her privately after the gathering to chat one-on-one.
Suggest a simple rule where everyone takes turns speaking in future meetings.

scenarios.title: An Angry Interruption
scenarios.setup_narrative: A listener angrily interrupts a poet who is reading a sensitive, personal poem. The poet freezes.

options.text: Point to the community guidelines on respect and introduce the next reader.
Walk up to stand beside the poet right away so they feel safe.
Pause the event and let the angry person briefly explain what upset them.
Ask everyone in the room to sit in quiet reflection for one minute.

scenarios.title: A Child Who Does Not Want to Paint
scenarios.setup_narrative: An 8-year-old boy refuses to paint. An experienced team volunteer whispers, 'Just leave him alone.'

options.text: Listen to your teammate's advice, but keep a watchful eye on the boy from where you stand.
Sit near him and draw quietly on your own paper so he feels no pressure.
Build a small tower out of paint jars to catch his interest.
Ask the full-time center staff what the boy usually enjoys doing.

scenarios.title: You Feel Very Tired
scenarios.setup_narrative: You feel very tired from a long week. A close friend is visiting your town for only one day, but you promised earlier to help set up today's event.

options.text: Keep your full promise to work. Meet your friend only if work finishes early.
Call the team leader honestly and offer to take a harder shift next week instead.
Invite your friend to come with you and help out as a guest volunteer.
Work the two hardest hours, hand over your jobs clearly to the team, and then leave.

stimuli_and_trials.title: Round 1: Rising Voice Line
stimuli_and_trials.cue_text: "The poet begins a rising, powerful verse."
stimuli_and_trials.baseline_context: Small Practice Room — Sound dies down quickly with no echo.

baseline_options.label: Support Volume
baseline_options.desc: Lift volume so sound carries across the room.

baseline_options.label: Lower Level
baseline_options.desc: Turn volume down before the loud peak.

baseline_options.label: Keep Steady
baseline_options.desc: Keep room settings steady without changes.

stimuli_and_trials.shifted_context: Stone Hall — High stone walls bounce sound and create heavy echo.

shifted_options.label: Lower Echo
shifted_options.desc: Trim room echo so words stay clear.

shifted_options.label: Support Volume
shifted_options.desc: Keep the volume boost from the small room.

shifted_options.label: Keep Steady
shifted_options.desc: Make no changes for the stone room.

stimuli_and_trials.title: Round 2: Quiet Whisper
stimuli_and_trials.cue_text: "The poet drops into a quiet whisper between lines."
stimuli_and_trials.baseline_context: Quiet Sitting Room — Audience sits close and easily hears every word.

baseline_options.label: Keep Natural Tone
baseline_options.desc: Keep sound soft and clear without extra volume.

baseline_options.label: High Boost
baseline_options.desc: Force the whisper to play at loud volume.

baseline_options.label: Mute Feed
baseline_options.desc: Treat quiet verse as dead sound.

stimuli_and_trials.shifted_context: Courtyard Gate — Nearby street chatter and fountain water cover soft voices.

shifted_options.label: Boost Voice
shifted_options.desc: Lift the voice so outdoor chatter does not hide it.

shifted_options.label: Keep Natural Tone
shifted_options.desc: Leave voice unboosted so whisper is hard to hear.

shifted_options.label: Mute Feed
shifted_options.desc: Treat quiet sound as an equipment issue.

stimuli_and_trials.title: Round 3: Pause Before Verse
stimuli_and_trials.cue_text: "The poet pauses suddenly before the final line."
stimuli_and_trials.baseline_context: Solo Recital — A single speaker recites at a steady, driving pace.

baseline_options.label: Keep Pace
baseline_options.desc: Keep the steady beat moving through the pause.

baseline_options.label: Stop Sound
baseline_options.desc: Stop all instruments abruptly on the pause.

baseline_options.label: Speed Up
baseline_options.desc: Push the recital forward past the pause.

stimuli_and_trials.shifted_context: Group Singing — A chorus enters during the pause to sing an answer line.

shifted_options.label: Make Space
shifted_options.desc: Pause instruments to let the chorus answer clearly.

shifted_options.label: Keep Pace
shifted_options.desc: Play straight through without waiting for the chorus.

stimuli_and_trials.title: Episode 1: The Master Painter’s Folio
stimuli_and_trials.ambiguity_text: An illuminated folio has gold dust borders and charcoal sketches. Two master painters worked during this era.
stimuli_and_trials.context_text: Records confirm Master Sadiq worked in Rainawari. He used willow-branch charcoal sketches and lapis blue borders.
stimuli_and_trials.decision_question: Attribute the folio maker and technique lineage:

choices.label: Master Sadiq (Rainawari workshop — willow charcoal sketch)
Master Habib (Palace court — imported graphite pencil)

stimuli_and_trials.title: Episode 2: The Exhibition Pavilion Ceiling
stimuli_and_trials.ambiguity_text: A carved ceiling panel displays woodwork styles from two different rebuilding periods.
stimuli_and_trials.context_text: Following the 1902 Dal Lake flood, builders used seasoned cedar wood. Earlier builders used soft river pine.
stimuli_and_trials.decision_question: Identify the structural timber and repair era:

choices.label: Post-1902 Flood Repair (Seasoned mountain cedar wood)

stimuli_and_trials.title: Trial 1: The Crisp Paper Fold
stimuli_and_trials.objective: Form a sharp, smooth crease on thick paper without tearing surface fibers.

tools.name: Polished Bone Tool
tools.affordance: Smooth curved edge that applies friction gently

tools.name: Steel Scribe Stylus
tools.affordance: Hard pointed needle tip for sharp indentation

tools.name: Beveled Bamboo Scraper
tools.affordance: Broad flat wooden face for broad surface pressure

methods.name: Firm Edge Pass
methods.desc: Slide rounded edge along ruler with continuous diagonal pressure.

methods.name: Flat Face Rub
methods.desc: Distribute wide surface friction across fold line.

methods.name: Sharp Point Drag
methods.desc: Draw tip directly across surface to score the fiber line.

bone_folder:firm_edge_pass.text: Clean, crisp burnished crease formed with zero surface abrasion.

bamboo_wedge:flat_face_rub.text: Smooth, even flattened fold achieved without marring surface grain.

metal_stylus:sharp_point_drag.text: Paper fibers sliced; sharp point cut through the paper fold.

metal_stylus:firm_edge_pass.text: Metal edge left dark metallic friction scuffs across the parchment.

bone_folder:flat_face_rub.text: Gentle, even crease formed; fibers compressed smoothly.

bamboo_wedge:firm_edge_pass.text: Uniform clean fold line established with natural wood contour.

bone_folder:sharp_point_drag.text: Uneven dragging motion; point dented paper surface.

bamboo_wedge:sharp_point_drag.text: Wood corner snagged on rough paper grain.

metal_stylus:flat_face_rub.text: Insufficient surface area; uneven pressure indentation.

stimuli_and_trials.title: Trial 2: Mulberry Paper Stipple
stimuli_and_trials.objective: Produce an even scatter of tiny ink drops on fibrous paper.

tools.name: Stiff Hair Brush
tools.affordance: Springy stiff bristles that snap back easily

tools.name: Natural Sea Sponge
tools.affordance: Soft porous texture that dabs damp color

tools.name: Rolled Cloth Swab
tools.affordance: Rolled fabric tip that absorbs liquid quickly

methods.name: Bristle Flick
methods.desc: Pull loaded bristles back with thumb to release fine mist.

methods.name: Surface Dab
methods.desc: Light stamp of textured surface directly on paper.

methods.name: Smooth Sweep
methods.desc: Draw applicator steadily across page in sweeping stroke.

horsehair_brush:textured_flick.text: Fine, even constellation of organic micro-droplets dispersed across parchment.

sponge_block:mottled_dab.text: Rich textured tonal stipple with soft, organic cellular grain.

linen_swab:drag_stroke.text: Produced a single continuous solid streak; zero stipple effect.

linen_swab:textured_flick.text: Fabric has no elastic bristle snap; pigment remained bound in swab.

sponge_block:drag_stroke.text: Smeared broad irregular smudge across paper.

horsehair_brush:drag_stroke.text: Solid brushstroke line created; no dispersed speckling.

horsehair_brush:mottled_dab.text: Bristle tips formed delicate speckled texture upon contact.

sponge_block:textured_flick.text: Sponge cannot be flicked; dropped heavy inconsistent blot.

linen_swab:mottled_dab.text: Dense blot soaked through fiber without texture.
